rule: A snapshot_platform test for a platform that contains entities with entity_registry_enabled_default=False must apply @pytest.mark.usefixtures("entity_registry_enabled_by_default"), because snapshot_platform asserts disabled_by is None for every entity.
trigger: A new or edited test calls snapshot_platform(hass, entity_registry, snapshot, entry.entry_id) for a platform whose entity descriptions include entity_registry_enabled_default=False, without the entity_registry_enabled_by_default fixture.
rationale: The shared snapshot helper asserts every registry entry is enabled, so a disabled-by-default entity silently fails the snapshot test rather than being captured.

evidence.excerpt: snapshot_platform helper asserts entity_entry.disabled_by is None for every entity

rule: Syrupy .ambr snapshot files must be produced by running pytest --snapshot-update; never hand-edit them or hand-append snapshot blocks.
trigger: A diff adds or modifies lines inside a tests/components/*/snapshots/*.ambr file in a way that deviates from generator output, e.g. a duplicated '# ---' divider or a manually written EntityRegistryEntrySnapshot block.
rationale: Deviations from the canonical generator output prove the snapshot was written by hand rather than captured from real entity state, so the snapshot no longer proves anything about the integration.

evidence.excerpt: regenerate with pytest --snapshot-update so the file matches canonical output
This extra line indicates the snapshot was hand-edited rather than produced by tooling

rule: An entity registry snapshot whose 'aliases' field renders as list([None]) must be investigated as an entity-registration bug; aliases must be an empty set or a set of non-null strings.
trigger: A new .ambr snapshot contains "'aliases': list([\n None,\n ])" inside an EntityRegistryEntrySnapshot.
rationale: Aliases are a set of strings in the entity registry; a None alias means the entity or its fixture is registering a null alias, and accepting the snapshot enshrines the bug.

evidence.excerpt: Entity aliases should be a set of strings, but snapshot shows list containing None
Having None in aliases suggests a bug in how the entity is registered

rule: A test that patches an API call to raise an authentication exception must assert that the reauth flow actually started (e.g. config_entry_reauth.assert_called_once()), not merely reference the mock.
trigger: A test injects an authentication exception via side_effect and references a reauth mock without calling an assertion method on it.
rationale: Without invoking the assertion the test passes even when reauth is never triggered, so the auth-failure path is untested.

evidence.excerpt: otherwise the test can pass even when reauth is never triggered

rule: Reconfigure-flow tests that submit only a subset of the config entry fields must assert that the omitted optional fields (credentials, tokens) are preserved on the entry.
trigger: A test_config_flow.py reconfigure test calls async_configure with a dict omitting CONF_USERNAME/CONF_PASSWORD or other optional entry keys and only asserts the flow result type.
rationale: A reconfigure flow that rewrites entry data can silently clear credentials the user never re-entered; only an explicit assertion catches that.

evidence.excerpt: ensure reconfigure does not unintentionally clear existing credentials when those optional fields are omitted

rule: When firing async_fire_time_changed to trigger a coordinator refresh, capture the base time after the config entries are set up (or add a margin / use fire_all=True); a time captured before setup can land before the timer the entity scheduled.
trigger: A test assigns now = dt_util.now()/utcnow() before async_setup_component or hass.config_entries.async_setup, then calls async_fire_time_changed(hass, now + <scan interval>) and asserts on refresh call counts.
rationale: The coordinator's next-refresh timer is only scheduled once an entity registers its listener, so a pre-setup timestamp makes the fired time earlier than the scheduled tick and the assertion flaky.

evidence.excerpt: coordinator's next refresh timer is scheduled later, making this assertion flaky

rule: A new mocked device/appliance fixture must configure every library accessor the integration's base entity reads, including the availability accessor, matching the sibling fixtures in the same conftest.
trigger: A conftest.py adds a Mock(spec=<device class>) fixture that sets some *.return_value attributes but omits one that existing fixtures for the same integration set (e.g. get_online.return_value = True).
rationale: The base entity derives availability from that accessor, so an unconfigured Mock returns a Mock object and the new device behaves differently from every other device in the same tests.

evidence.excerpt: missing get_online return value, used by base WhirlpoolEntity class to determine entity availability

rule: Config entry migration tests must be named (and their docstring worded) for the exact version transition exercised, e.g. test_migrate_minor_version_1_to_2 rather than test_migrate_to_1_1.
trigger: A test in tests/components/*/test_init.py exercises async_migrate_entry / minor_version or version bumps but its name does not state the source and target version.
rationale: Entry version and minor_version are distinct axes; an ambiguous name hides which migration path is actually covered as more migrations accumulate.

evidence.excerpt: Rename this test to reflect the actual minor-version migration being exercised

rule: Fixtures that build a MockConfigEntry must derive its title, data and options from the parametrizable config fixture rather than hard-coding literals.
trigger: A conftest.py fixture constructs MockConfigEntry(domain=DOMAIN, title="<literal>", ...) while a sibling get_config/mock_config fixture supplies the same value and can be overridden by tests.
rationale: Tests that override the config fixture then get an entry whose title disagrees with its options, making entity IDs and device names diverge from the configuration under test.

evidence.excerpt: Derive the MockConfigEntry title from get_config[CONF_TIME_ZONE] instead of hard-coding it

rule: Tests must address entities by their hard-coded entity ID (as captured in the snapshot) instead of looking the ID up dynamically from the entity registry.
trigger: A test calls er.async_entries_for_config_entry(...) and filters by domain/platform just to recover a single entity_id for a service call or state assertion.
rationale: Home Assistant's testing conventions favor the literal entity ID: it is shorter, it is already pinned by the snapshot, and the registry fixture plus explanatory comment become unnecessary.

evidence.excerpt: Per the repo's testing conventions, hardcoding the entity ID is fine and clearer

rule: Test docstrings must state only the behavior under test; do not narrate device model history, the prior bug, or the PR description in them.
trigger: A new test's docstring spans multiple paragraphs describing a specific device firmware quirk, the exception it used to raise, or the regression history.
rationale: The setup, assertions and PR description already carry that context, so the narrative duplicates them and goes stale.

evidence.excerpt: Shorten this docstring to state only the behavior under test

rule: Behavioral tests for a trigger must exercise every entity domain the trigger implementation accepts, not just one of them.
trigger: New tests for a zone/state/entity trigger parametrize over a single domain (e.g. "person") while the trigger's implementation also handles device_tracker or other domains.
rationale: Domain filtering and in_zones handling differ per domain, so regressions in the untested domain go unnoticed.

evidence.excerpt: trigger implementation explicitly supports both person and device_tracker, but tests only exercise person

rule: Changes to shared trigger/helper base classes must add coverage for subclasses that intentionally target STATE_UNKNOWN/STATE_UNAVAILABLE before excluding those states globally.
trigger: A diff makes an EntityTriggerBase-style helper skip unavailable/unknown states in match logic, and the accompanying tests only use an implementation whose is_valid_state() rejects those states.
rationale: BEHAVIOR_FIRST/BEHAVIOR_LAST semantics differ for triggers that legitimately fire on unknown or unavailable, and a blanket exclusion silently breaks them.

evidence.excerpt: confirm the new exclusion logic doesn't break BEHAVIOR_FIRST/BEHAVIOR_LAST for triggers targeting those states

rule: A fix for an async race must ship a regression test that actually drives both concurrent call paths; asserting a new private flag (e.g. script_obj._unloaded) does not substitute for reproducing the race.
trigger: A PR adds unload/teardown guard state to a helper and its test only asserts the private attribute instead of starting a run while the unload is in progress.
rationale: Unload and start requests originate from independent async call points, so the race is simulable; without that test the guard's observable contract (no raise, no stale hass.data entry) stays unverified.

evidence.excerpt: Add a regression test that exercises the reported unload race
unload and start requests can originate from different async call points

rule: Test cases added to the custom pylint quality-scale checkers must encode a rule the checker deliberately enforces; incidental matches produced by the implementation should be dropped or the implementation adjusted.
trigger: A new parametrized case in tests/pylint/quality_scale/ asserts a diagnostic on code whose flagged condition cannot occur in practice (e.g. _attr_unique_id assignment after a raise in __init__).
rationale: Locking in a side effect of the checker implementation turns an accident into a contract; the reviewers ask whether the case reflects an intended rule before it is enshrined in tests.

evidence.excerpt: If catching this just a sideeffect of your implementation, I would remove the test

rule: Changes to the split_tests fixture-hashing logic must add coverage proving the hash changes when a shared helper module above or beside the chosen root is edited, not only for conftest.py files.
trigger: A diff modifies fixture-hash computation in script/split_tests and its tests only cover conftest.py edits and same-directory scope.
rationale: Stale cached test counts after a shared-helper edit produce wrong subtree splits, and only an ancestor-helper case catches that invalidation gap.

evidence.excerpt: ensure subtree runs invalidate cached counts correctly
asserts the descendant test file's fixture hash changes, to prevent stale cache hits

rule: End-to-end frontend tests must assert on the element of the specific step under test, not on the outer shell component that renders before its API call resolves.
trigger: A Playwright spec asserts only expect(page.locator("ha-onboarding")).toBeVisible() (or another shell element) after navigating, without waiting for the concrete step element.
rationale: The shell renders a loading card before /api/onboarding resolves, so the assertion passes even when the API request fails.

evidence.excerpt: ha-onboarding renders a visible loading card before /api/onboarding resolves
